eval:design.verdict:
v2 is a real step up. It does more than tidy v1: it moves the source of fun. The minute loop now ends in consequences that recur. Nine systemic rules with a priority order (§9-2, §9-3) replace one-off gags. Density is now built per zone rather than per chapter: 3 sub-gimmicks per chapter, intro→apply→twist→graduate every 10-15 minutes, 66 garnish objects, and main length cut to about 4.4 h. The controls conflicts are fixed (latch carry, hold-to-throw, facing = placement direction, jump = cancel). The tug can now actually fail, and it has visible outcomes. Retention gates at 1/10/30 min and 2 h measure the original complaint directly. Four problems remain.

(1) The tug is a contest in form more than in substance. I simulated the §5-3 formula. Any player who simply lets go during resist phases ends at 60 points ('좋음'). Anyone who hits the hook gets 91-100 ('딱!') on every type and grade. So the top tier depends on one press at a fixed, memorisable time, and analog trigger depth barely matters.

(2) The 10-30 min loop is still a gate corridor. Zone goals are almost always 'open the gate', and the emergent chains in §9-3 mostly end in 'crowd = weight on a plate'. Nothing like the player-chosen to-do list that drives Untitled Goose Game exists.

(3) Chapter 4, the emotional climax at hours 3.5-4.4, adds almost no new mechanics. It re-teaches stake locks from chapter 1's first 90 seconds. Meanwhile chapter 3 is overloaded, and the §10-4 density table counts look-only variants and scene cards, so it overstates.

(4) Tension beats exist in every chapter, but none has a consequence lasting longer than a few seconds.

The first 75 seconds contain about one input, which is risky against a 5-of-5 one-minute gate. As written, I expect the first hour to be genuinely good and a sag around hour 3-4 to be possible, but no longer likely.
strengths: The source of fun moves from pulling to consequences (§1 '재미의 중심', §9). The two-layer reaction design (a one-time gag saved as a scene card, plus rules that fire every time) fixes the 'fifth mailbox' problem directly. The nine rules work like Untitled Goose Game's NPC routines and have a stated priority order: owners follow their objects, animals gather at heat, neighbours gather at light or shade, freed things follow you, a crowd counts as weight, bells call neighbours. Chains like 'hot stone → cat and chickens sleep → crowd presses the plate' (§9-3) are surprises nobody has to script.

The tug is rebuilt with real failure and real outcomes (§5). I re-simulated the §5-3 formula and it matches the doc's own table. Just holding the trigger now fails on every catfish target and on carp XL, eel L/XL (without counter-steer) and puffer L/XL, so the rhythm matters. Hidden assists are gone. The v1 auto-weakening is now the visible '손이 익었다' rule (thicker wrist wrap). Sparkle soil is a one-shot skill stake (1/2/3 seeds, then it is gone). Mastery fast-pluck after 5 good pulls and a target of 12-20 full pulls per chapter keep the tug from becoming homework.

The controls contract (§4) fixes every v1 conflict. Carry is latched, so no thumb has to hold two buttons. Throw is hold-and-release, so there are no stick-flick misfires. Placement faces the way Ongi faces, with an arrow in the preview, which makes the wind, light, bounce and mirror puzzles playable. Jump cancels a tug with no penalty. S versus M+ is decided by grade, not press length. Line-up pulls use the same input as a normal tug, and the 'Yeongcha!' beat is a signal, not a judgement.

Density is now designed at the right grain (§12-2, §10-2): 3 sub-gimmicks per chapter, each 10-15 minute zone running the full four-step cycle, minute-by-minute beat sheets for chapters 0-1, 66 garnish rows that reuse archetype animations, and the stated rule 'if density fails, shorten the main game rather than pad it'. This is the Donut County / A Short Hike lesson applied.

Tag combos are now verbs, not range buffs (§8-2). All 8 named combos create a new action (launch, dam, windbreak, sweeping beam, steam column, rainbow bridge, water current, inflate). Results never chain, and undefined pairs are explicitly 'no reaction'. Light now has dark spaces to work in (cellars, caves, fog). This keeps the TotK-style 'right property works' promise without rigid-body chaos (§16-4).

The procession is no longer an escort mission (§7-4). It walks paths you have already cleared on its own while you scout ahead, which is real Pikmin-style parallel play. Conditional path edges are judged by property, so unintended solutions work. Teleporting happens only on AI error, segments last 30-90 s, and obstacles take 1-2 moves to clear.

The protagonist feeds the design. Ongi's body is the tension gauge: root-toes lift one by one, the wrist thread heats up, the straw bristles (§5-3). That removes the HUD gauge and supports 'teach without text'. Starting the game by plucking yourself out of the ground puts the theme into the very first input (§3-6).

There is now a tension budget per chapter (§12-9): a moving set piece, a timed window, an undoer and a social consequence in every chapter. Social consequences now start in chapter 1 (§9-4) rather than appearing only in chapter 5.
The original complaint is now measured directly: stop/continue cards at 1/10/30 min and 2 h, quit-point telemetry, and a 2-hour gate on chapter 2-3 builds (§20-6, §19-6).

issues.section: §5-3 formula, §5-4 pull score / grades, §4-1 analog grab
issues.problem: The outcome tier comes down to a single press at a fixed time. I simulated §5-3 as written. A player who just goes full in tired phases and fully slack in resist phases never slips and always scores 60 ('좋음'): the in-grain ratio is 100% and the finish lands in a tired phase. Adding the hook gives 91-100 ('딱!') for every type and grade (carp M 0.58 s/100, catfish XL 4.1 s/92, eel XL 2.0 s/98). So the '결 따라' and '마무리' terms almost never separate players. The 딱! tier, which brings glossy variants, 3 seeds and maximum size, is decided by one input at a fixed delay (0.6/0.9/0.5/0.7 s) that becomes muscle memory within a few pulls. Analog depth hardly matters: the best play is binary, so the face-button remap plays the same, and the keyboard Shift '살살' (50%) option is pointless. The doc also calls the faster partial-pull style '숙련', yet the score formula rewards the slower full-release style, so it never decides what mastery means. Carp M, the most common M type and the only M type allowed for garnish, is beaten by simply holding the trigger.
issues.fix: Make tension control the skill, keeping the hook as one input to the score. (a) Make tension rise with d² while progress scales with d, so a 30-60% pull in resist is efficient and safe up to a point. That creates a real sweet band, as in fishing-drag games, and gives the trigger an actual job. (b) Score = hook 25 + time spent in the 'green band' (T between 0.5 and 0.85) 50 + finish on a tired beat 25. Holding near the limit without slipping becomes the expert play, readable from the root-toes (3-4 lifted = sweet spot). (c) Shift the 툭 timing by environment and instance (wet −0.1 s, frozen +0.15 s, sparkle-soil roots get a double 툭) so the hook stays a read, not a memorised beat. (d) Keep 'just hold' succeeding on carp M on purpose (the ritual floor), but say so in §5-1.

issues.problem: The difficulty curve sags exactly where emotion peaks. Chapter 4 (50 min, hours 3.5-4.4) brings 1 new archetype, 0 new tags or combos, and a rule 8 variant. Two of its three sub-gimmicks are re-teaches: the stake lock is introduced in chapter 1's first 90 seconds (§12-4 1-1), and a pulled stake 'remains as a weight object' from then on (§6-3). The third, moving a house whole, uses the L procession the player has used since chapter 2. Chapter 3 meanwhile teaches 4 combos plus tide, spreading frost, hanging objects and the mirror in 55 minutes. §10-4 makes the density look better than it is by counting look-only variants (wind-leaning variants are '겉모습만'), scene cards (a by-product of each new archetype's first gag) and garnish as 'new things'. Counting only new archetypes, rules or combos and set pieces gives about 1.3 / 2.6 / 3.1 / 5.0 / 8.3 minutes per new mechanic for chapters 0-4. Only chapters 0-2 have minute-level beat sheets.
issues.fix: (1) Take the stake out of chapter 1 1-1: open the field gate with a plate or a seized rope instead, so chapter 4 owns stakes. (2) Move inflate (heat + elastic) and/or mirror plus rainbow bridge from chapter 3 into chapter 4. For example, float a tilted house over a stake fence on a heat-inflated mushroom, or light the underground waterway with the mirror. That also eases chapter 3. (3) Add one chapter 4 rule that only works with stakes: stakes in a chained network pass load along the chain, so pulling one tilts whichever house its neighbour holds. That makes an ordering puzzle that also carries the story. (4) Drop look-only variants and scene cards from the §10-4 metric, report the strict count alongside, and set a ceiling of 5 minutes per new mechanic. (5) Write minute-level beat sheets for chapters 2-4 before the vertical slice, not after.

issues.section: §1 three loop layers (10-15 min), §9-3, §12-4 to §12-7 zone goals
issues.problem: The 10-30 minute loop is a linear row of gates, and the systemic rules mostly feed one kind of lock. Nearly every graduation step is 'open the gate / road', and 'plate' appears 16 times in the chapter beat tables. Five of the eight emergent examples in §9-3 end in rule 5 (crowd = weight) pressing a plate or sinking a floor. The '이웃의 그림말 부탁' promised in the §1 loop table never appears in any zone design. Neighbour requests exist only as 10 village wishes. Goose Game's real 10-30 minute engine is a visible list of player-chosen goals in each area, solvable in any order and by several routes. Here the player has no choice of goal, only of method, and 'press the plate' risks becoming the new single verb.
issues.fix: Give every zone a 부탁 board of 3-5 small requests, drawn with the existing wish pictogram system (§13-3 already budgets a week for it). Examples: cat wants a warm nap spot, farmer wants the dry field watered, guests want a sea view, kids want a bounce pad. Each request should be solvable through at least 2 rule or tag routes and pay out a scene card plus 1-2 seeds. Require any 2 of the zone's requests for graduation, so the player picks which. Widen what rule outputs can unlock: a gathered crowd opens a 'crossable' path edge (neighbours form a human chain), sleeping animals block wind as a windbreak, a bell crowd starts an event or market, a lit area makes a shy neighbour appear. Cap plates at roughly one in three of each zone's locks.

issues.problem: The original failure was 'quit after one minute', yet the first 75 seconds hold about one input. 0:00-0:20 has no input. 0:20-0:45 is a scripted self-pluck that cannot fail. 0:45-1:15 is a 30-second cutscene of grandma weaving the gloves. Free S-plucking starts at 1:15, so the 1-minute stop/continue card lands in the middle of a cutscene. The beats are lovely, but they are trailer pacing, not first-play pacing.
issues.fix: Keep non-interactive time under about 10 s before the first free input. Trim the sound-only black screen to 3-4 s. Make the glove gift interactive: Ongi plucks loose straw tufts (S) from the gate's 금줄 while grandma ties them on bit by bit, so the gloves grow during the first S-pluck tutorial. Free S-plucking with visible consequences (bugs, ants, the cat) should start by 0:30. Show the first scene card before 1:00, and move the 1-minute card to a moment of play.

issues.section: §4-2 input table, §17-1 three on-screen overlays, §6-4 outlines, §12-3 teaching
issues.problem: There are new controls gaps that will cause 'why doesn't this work?'. (1) Grab targeting is never defined, and no target highlight exists. §17-1 allows only three overlays, and every pluckable already has an ink outline (§6-4), so in a dense garnish cluster the player can't tell what grab will act on. (2) 'Empty hand + grab on empty ground while a procession moves = plant a flag' will misfire whenever a grab narrowly misses an S object, sending the procession somewhere else. (3) Rotate-in-place uses a stick tilt under 35%, which keyboard WASD can't do and which is fragile around deadzones. (4) The hook means dipping the trigger below 70% and squeezing again within 0.2 s, but grab has just been pressed to 100% to attach. Nothing in the world teaches 'loosen, then squeeze', and the 0-chapter jar beat at 11:30 assumes the player discovers it. (5) Hold-to-throw is not discoverable from a tap glyph alone.
issues.fix: (1) Grab acts on the facing cell, then the nearest pluckable in a 45° cone in front. Add a fourth overlay: a glove icon or outline pulse on the current target. (2) Planting a flag takes a 0.5 s hold on empty ground with a filling ring. A miss-tap then does nothing. (3) Add LB/RB (Q/E) as 'rotate 90°', a utility like the look stick. Keep the soft-tilt rotate as an extra. (4) Use the natural fishing strike: after the grab press the glove stays attached even if the player lets go, and the hook is the first squeeze from below 20% within 0.2 s of the 툭. Players instinctively ease off and then yank. (5) At the 0-chapter ditch, show a hold glyph with a filling circle the first three times the player carries an S object near an unplaceable edge.

issues.problem: Every chapter now has tension beats, but none has a consequence lasting longer than seconds, so they read as scenery. A boulder hit costs 1 cell. The tide regrows anything carried off. The broom undoes a 15-second task. Chapter 4's social stakes are cosmetic as well: a tilted house has no clock, and §13-1 auto-plants any unplaced house at the end of the village stage, so 'the owner refuses to line up' never actually matters. Goose Game keeps tension through being caught and chased, Pikmin through the day clock. No death is fine, but tension that costs nothing at all fades by chapter 2.
issues.fix: Add outcomes that can be missed but can be recovered or replaced, without ever blocking progress. Chapter 4: a house keeps tilting slowly in steps (it never breaks). If the player doesn't reach it, the family climbs out to safety and the 'family inside' moment and its scene card are lost for that house, though a later house offers a second chance. Chapter 3: un-anchored objects the tide carries off regrow, but the sparkle soil on them is gone. Make the sparkle one-shot rule visible in the world (the soil glows a little less after a weak pull). Give each chapter's moving set piece a tiny optional reward for a clean run (a scene card or seed for never getting flattened in the boulder chase). Keep everything off the critical path.

issues.section: §5-4 손에 익음 vs glossy variant and size record
issues.problem: After 5 'good' pulls a type is mastered and always fast-plucks with a fixed 'good' result, except on sparkle-soil instances. A player who masters a type before ever hitting '딱!' can then only earn its glossy variant or a better size record from sparkle instances, and some types may have none. That is a silent lock-out ('why can't I get the shiny one anymore?'), which breaks the 'eliminate why doesn't this work' principle.
issues.fix: Award the ★ only after one '딱!' on that type, or count 5 good pulls including one 딱. Alternatively, guarantee at least one sparkle-soil instance of every archetype in the game and let the field guide show which types still lack a glossy.

issues.problem: The village is the long-loop showcase (Katamari's 'the things you collected become a world'), but tags there are judged only as static ranges and no rules run. Animals don't gather at your hot stones and neighbours don't drift to your lanterns or shade. It becomes a grid decorator with 10 wish checks for 4-5 minutes per chapter, and the systems the player spent hours learning go quiet exactly where expression should peak.
issues.fix: Run the attractor rules (1, 2, 3, 4, 9) in the village. They are cheap pathing to points of interest and need no tag motion. Water, wind and melting can stay static. The village then becomes an ant farm of your layout: a lantern lane fills with neighbours at dusk, cats nap by the inn's hearth. Add one 'village event' per stage that fires from a rule chain the player set up.

issues.problem: Scale growth arrives only at chapter ends (a grip stage per boss, a landmark per chapter). Katamari's engine is the threshold moment every few minutes ('now I can take that'). Inside a chapter, what the player can pull never grows.
issues.fix: Use the existing rainbow grammar ('rainbow = N neighbours') for 1-2 small rainbow objects per chapter (N=2-4) mid-chapter, unlocked by gathering the entourage or freed animals in that chapter. Rescuing someone then pays off within minutes, and the grammar stays intact.

issues.problem: After the first of each type, a garnish pluck gives nothing: the hole is cosmetic, there are no seeds, and the field guide entry is already filled. Law 2 ('there is always something under the root') teaches anticipation, but players will learn within about 20 minutes that most holes are empty, and the 'unprompted grabs per minute' metric will drop. Bananza and Donut County keep a reward every few seconds.
issues.fix: Author a deterministic 'pocket' under about one garnish in every 6-8 per cluster (a collectible, a letter fragment, an animal), cued by Ongi's resonance hum (§3-5) getting louder as you approach. This keeps the curiosity without randomness and costs only data rows using pocket prefab ②.

issues.problem: The broom returns your most recently placed M object 15 seconds later. If that happens off-screen or behind the player, the object simply 'isn't there', which reads as a bug rather than a prank.
issues.fix: Only allow the undo while the object is on-screen. Telegraph it: a sweeping sound and a peeking broom 3 s before, and the broom visibly dragging the object back. If the object is off-screen, the broom waits beside it.

issues.problem: Knots are sold as 'changing how you play', but they are conveniences with no trade-off. '이슬' (always wet) and '들여다보기' (preview under root) are pure information and will be worn permanently, so 'one knot at a time' isn't a real choice.
issues.fix: Make every knot cost something or open a traversal option. For example: a light knot (Ongi is pushed by wind, a new route but harder in gusts), a deep-root knot (anything you place can't be undone by the broom but needs a full tug to move again), a twin knot that can't carry M. Or fold the information knots into the base kit.

issues.problem: Moving around has no joy of its own: 3.2 m/s walk, 1.1 m jump, and gliding only with a carried mushroom in chapter 2. A Short Hike's minute loop is largely movement, and here travelling between plucks is dead time.
issues.fix: Make the existing 데굴 roll pose a movement verb with no new button: walking empty-handed down a slope tips Ongi onto his side to roll fast, cell by cell and deterministically. Floating downstream should feel like a ride. Both are cheap and on-theme.

eval:design.v1IssuesResolved:
All 13 v1 design-lens issues, in order.

1. Critical: one-off gags and untagged objects. RESOLVED: the two layers plus 9 systemic rules (§9). A new, smaller problem: the rules mostly end in pressure plates.
2. Critical: density, one gimmick per chapter. LARGELY RESOLVED in structure (3 sub-gimmicks, 10-15 min zones, 66 garnish, 4.4 h). STILL OPEN for chapter 4 (almost no new mechanics) and chapter 3 (overloaded). The §10-4 metric overstates density.
3. Critical: fishing as ritual, not contest. PARTIAL: failure exists, hidden assists are gone, and outcomes exist (sparkle, glossy, size, landing, mastery). But the 딱! tier depends only on the fixed-time hook, and analog depth barely matters (my simulation of §5-3).
4. Major: controls overload. MOSTLY RESOLVED (latch, hold-throw, cancel, grade split). New gaps: grab targeting and highlight, flag misfire, keyboard rotation, hook not teachable without text.
5. Major: placement orientation. RESOLVED (facing plus arrow, §4-2, §7-2), apart from the keyboard rotation gap.
6. Major: combos that only extend range, and nowhere for light to work. RESOLVED (§8-2, §8-3).
7. Major: procession as escort. RESOLVED (autopilot plus scouting, wait points, Yeongcha march, §7-4). Still linear, with one procession at a time.
8. Major: thin long loop. PARTIAL: the cart showcase, knots, seed economy and landmark escalation are added. The village has no running rules and knots are conveniences.
9. Major: no tension. PARTIAL: per-chapter beats exist (§12-9), but none carries a lasting consequence, and chapter 4's social stakes are cancelled by auto-planting.
10. Minor: line-up trigger and a third timing system. RESOLVED (§5-6).
11. Minor: randomness muddle. RESOLVED (§5-1, §5-4).
12. Minor: regrowth. RESOLVED (§15-4).
13. Minor: retention metrics. RESOLVED (1/10/30 min and 2 h gates plus telemetry, §20-6, §19-6).
topRecommendations: Build the 10-30 minute loop around goals the player chooses. Give each zone a Goose-style 부탁 board of 3-5 pictogram requests, reusing the §13-3 wish icons. Each request should be solvable by at least 2 rule or tag routes, and graduation should need any 2. Widen what systemic rules can unlock beyond plates: neighbour chains as crossable path edges, sleeping animals as windbreaks, bell crowds triggering events. Cap plates at about a third of each zone's locks.

Re-tune the §5-3 and §5-4 tug so mastery means tension control, not a memorised hook. Make tension rise with d² while progress scales with d, so a gentle pull has a real sweet band and analog depth matters. Score = hook 25 + time in the green band 50 + finish on a tired beat 25. Shift the 툭 timing with environment and instance. Make the hook 'the first squeeze from released' (the natural fishing strike). Award the mastery ★ only after one 딱!, so glossy variants are never silently locked away.

Fix the chapter 3→4 curve before the vertical slice. Take the stake lock out of chapter 1's 1-1 so chapter 4 owns stakes. Move inflate and/or mirror plus rainbow bridge into chapter 4 (for example, lift tilted houses over stake fences on an inflated mushroom). Add a chapter 4 stake-network rule where pulling one stake moves the load to chained stakes. Re-count density strictly, without look-only variants or scene cards, with a ceiling of 5 minutes per new mechanic, and write minute-level beat sheets for chapters 2-4.

Protect the first minute and close the controls gaps. Keep non-interactive time under about 10 s, make the glove gift playable, and start free S-plucking by 0:30. Add a target highlight as a fourth overlay, a 0.5 s hold to plant a flag, LB/RB (Q/E) to rotate 90°, and a hold glyph for throwing.

Give soft tension outcomes that can be missed but recovered. Chapter 4 houses tilt in steps and you can miss the 'family inside' moment. Sparkle soil and clean set-piece runs give small one-shot rewards. Let attractor rules 1-4 and 9 run in the village, so the long-loop showcase is alive, which is the Katamari payoff. Add small mid-chapter rainbow objects (N=2-4) for threshold moments within each chapter.

eval:production.verdict: From a production and tech point of view, v2 is a large step up from v1. It now has an actual pipeline: a grid diorama, text/JSON levels, an auto preview, a solver bot, kinematic deterministic puzzle physics, a cost-tier column with caps, a reuse table that names real files (I checked that the paths exist), a perf budget, gates with 2 hard checks each, and an honest schedule of 17-18 months with a re-forecast after the vertical slice. With the Steam-only decision, keeping three.js/Electron is clearly right, and the old repo already builds Linux and Windows depots (tools/package-steam.mjs). The main remaining problem: v2 cut the number of chapters but raised content density per chapter about 2-3x, and it still prices each chapter at the v1 review's 7 weeks. v1 had 28 objects. v2 has 31 archetypes, 66 garnish, 23 variants, 10 decorations, 9 system rules, 8 combos, about 24 named neighbours each a different species, tides, a boulder chase and a walking boss you can climb. The world model (one height per cell, §16-1) can't represent the cellars, tunnels, ceiling cells, bridges and walkable object tops the design depends on. The solver bot as specified is not tractable, and one of its checks passes automatically. The vertical slice and the week-6 check skip the riskiest tech (layered holes, moving platforms, camera-zone rotation, wind/tide state, carrying a 2x3 or bigger object through the level), so the costs measured there won't predict chapters 2-4. The owner's weekly time budget covers play and judging only, not reviewing art or marketing, and the buffer is about 8%. Realistic outcome: shippable, probably in spring or summer 2028 rather than Feb-Mar, unless the trims are decided in advance now.
strengths: §16-1/§19-3: the 1 m grid + 0.5 m height diorama, ASCII height/cell maps plus JSON object lists, an auto preview on every save, and an explicit 'no in-game editor' rule. Together they fix v1's biggest hidden cost (no way to author levels). The '2 days to a playable greybox' check is a measurable test of the pipeline.

§16-4: the kinematic, deterministic physics table (roll tile by tile at 4 tiles/s, fixed throw arcs with landing snap, fixed bounce height, water as a channel graph, a sinking floor that can be pulled back up, 'fall-up' only at object level, physics for cosmetic debris only). It is concrete enough for agents to implement and test without guessing.

§10-1/§10-3/§20-2: every row has a cost tier (A 0.5 d / B 2-4 d / C level work) with caps of 16/8/8, there are 6 reusable hole prefabs, garnish must borrow archetype motion and stay under 0.5 d, and variants are colour/pose-only at 0.25 d. Those are exactly the levers a solo-plus-agents team needs, and the doc names downgrading B/C to A as the overflow valve.

§20-7: the schedule is itemised and honest. 7 weeks per chapter is broken down, the 47.5 remaining weeks are listed by line item, release slips to month 17-18, and there is a trigger to move Next Fest to October if the vertical slice runs past week 20. It also names the owner's play/judging time as the real constraint.

§20-5: the vertical slice is 'one of every repeatable content type at final quality', with a table of per-type build times to measure and then re-forecast from. This follows the v1 production review's recommendation directly.

§20-6: phase gates now have 2 hard checks and tracked metrics, results are counted ('4 of 5') rather than given as fake percentages, a failed gate is re-checked with 5 new testers, and there are quit/continue cards at 1, 10, 30 and 120 minutes that measure the original 'quit after a minute' problem directly.

§19-2: the reuse table uses real paths (src/render/uproot.ts 938 lines, raccoon.ts, feel.ts, camera.ts, occlusion.ts, quality.ts, audio dsp/mixer/sequencer/sfxkit, platform, electron/, tools/layout-svg.ts, model-selftest.ts), has a 'what to fix' column, and an explicit leave-behind list (src/sim, src/ai, match flow, menu3d).

§7-4: the procession moves on an authored graph with conditional edges judged by cell properties (not object names), has wait points, teleports only on AI error, runs one procession at a time and shows at most 12 bearers. That bounds the system that was riskiest in v1.

§11-1: one shared 3-phase dokkaebi state machine plus one bespoke behaviour per boss, budgeted at 1.5-2 weeks each, with bosses cut from 5 to 4. §12-1/§20-1 drop the gravity-flip chapter permanently and set a cut order (chapter 3 first, chapter 4 last).

§18-3/§19-5/§19-6: numeric perf budget (under 300 draws, under 500k tris, 60 fps on Steam Deck, 40 Hz fallback), instancing per type with an automated harness built from model-selftest, a fixed-timestep sim with timestamped and recorded inputs, and a telemetry spec that includes an observer 'why?' hotkey (F8).

§24 does not make up any video content and gives a clean intake procedure (title + 3-line note per video → principle table → affected chapters → re-review of only those parts). §23 keeps all 7 of the owner's video principles.

issues.problem: The 7 weeks per chapter in §20-7 is the v1 review's estimate for v1-density chapters (one gimmick, about 5 objects). v2 chapters are 3-4 zones × 3 sub-gimmicks × 4 stages each. Each chapter adds 12-16 garnish, 5-11 variants, 1-3 new named neighbours of new species, 2-4 rules/combos, timer mechanics (tides, the boulder chase, frost spreading) and a boss. That is roughly 2-3x the content per chapter. Rough count: archetypes 16×0.5 d + 8×3 d, garnish 66×0.5 d, variants 23×0.25 d, about 24 neighbour models and pose sets, about 40 scene cards. That is about 90-120 agent-days of content, and every item still needs the owner's review. None of it was re-priced. The buffer is 4 of 47.5 weeks (about 8%), and the December 2027 holidays are not counted.
issues.fix: Plan 9-10 weeks per chapter until the vertical slice measures otherwise. That puts the release build around April-May 2028, or else decide the trims now: garnish 66→40, variants 23→12, named neighbours 15+9 optional→12+4 built on 2-3 shared body templates with species-specific heads, scene cards about 40→25. Raise the buffer to 15-20% and add the 2027 holidays. Put a 'content-days' line per chapter next to the 7-week breakdown so the vertical-slice re-forecast is mechanical.

issues.section: §16-1 world model / §19-3 level format vs §10-3 ⑤⑥, §12-6 3-3, §11-2, §7-2
issues.problem: §16-1 says each cell has one height and one cell type, and the format has only [height] and [cell] grids. But the design needs space above or below other walkable space: cellars 'one level below' (⑥), tunnel pairs (⑤), sea caves and underground waterways, a 'ceiling cell' layer in 3-3, bridges over water, the lighthouse's 1st-floor railing and seaward window, the windmill roof axle you glide onto, the iron-stake giant's back, the flat-top stacking rule and standing on placed objects. A heightfield cannot express any of these. This is the core of the pipeline and it is undefined.
issues.fix: Define an area as one or more grid 'decks', each a heightfield with its own cell grid, linked by portals (stairs, hole entry cells, ladders), plus a 'walkable top' footprint for objects that have a height. Hole prefabs ⑤/⑥ instantiate a small authored sub-room deck behind a portal; they don't carve the main heightfield. Extend the ASCII format with [deck N] sections and a portal list. Prototype a cellar, a tunnel pair and a ceiling cell as greybox in weeks 4-6, before the format freezes.

issues.problem: Exhaustive search over 'every moved object's cell, facing and state plus flags' is intractable once there are 10-20 movable objects in an area. Timers (plank 6 s, rainbow bridge 8 s, fog 20 s, tide 90/30 s, broom dokkaebi 15 s, boulder chase 6 s) and NPC rules (rule 5: two or more neighbours or animals count as weight on a plate) also make the state time- and AI-dependent. Check 3 ('from every reachable state you can reach the zone goal or the reset stump') always passes, because §15-5's stump is reachable from every state.
issues.fix: Search only over objects tagged as puzzle-relevant in the level JSON (everything else is scenery to the solver). Model NPC and animal rules as a deterministic 'settle' function that resolves to cell assignments with fixed tie-breaks. Model timers as windows that are either 'open' or 'closed'. Change check 3 to 'goal reachable without the stump' and log the near-dead-end states found, so the stump becomes a measured safety net rather than a proof. Give each area a CI time budget, and fall back to replaying authored solutions plus a bounded random walk when search runs out of time. Add a per-plate flag saying whether crowds count, so authors keep control.

issues.problem: Cost tiers cover only Pluckables. The actor layer is unpriced: about 24 named neighbours, each a different species ('don't make a herd of one species'); about 10 animal kinds; poses (walk, carry overhead, point, cheer, sit, sulk, sleep, follow, hold the rope); grid pathfinding for wandering NPCs that move to heat, shade, light or calls and step out of the way of rolls and throws; a priority scheduler; and pictogram bubbles. Twelve bearers of different species also defeat the 'instancing + shader animation' plan in §18-3. Instancing works per mesh type, so 12 species means about 12× the part draws. Several rows marked A also have secondary actors: #2 ants with signs, #4 neighbours clapping, #20 goat climbing the roof, #27 bird flock. So the real B count is above the cap of 8.
issues.fix: Add an actor cost table: neighbour = shared body template (2-3 shapes) + species head/ear/colour parameters + one shared pose library (about 0.5-1 d each); animals ≤ 5 kinds in the release build. Re-tier rows #2, #4, #20, #27 (or make their gags particle-only). Build the NPC rule engine as its own vertical-slice line item, with rules 1, 2, 4, 5 measured.

issues.problem: The procession runs on an authored node/edge graph, but the player can plant a straw flag on any empty cell as the destination, and an authored graph can't reach arbitrary cells. Clearance for carried footprints (L 2×2-2×3, XL 3×3-4×4) is undefined, so it's unclear whether a 4-wide object needs a 4-wide path. The default destination is the chapter's moving gate, but chapters are 3-4 zones: what happens when the procession has to cross zone boundaries while the player is ahead, or when zones load separately? Hand-authoring nodes, edges, conditional edges and wait points per zone is also real level-design time that §20-7 doesn't count.
issues.fix: Generate the procession graph automatically from the grid using a clearance map per footprint width. Derive conditional edges from cells marked 'crossable', and keep only wait points and gate nodes hand-authored. Restrict straw flags to cells the clearance graph can reach (the ghost turns grey otherwise). Define zone crossing: when the procession reaches a zone's exit node, the object is banked to the moving gate (like the cart in §6-5), and the next zone starts with a short procession from its entry node.

issues.problem: The slice and the week-6 check cover chapter 0-1 tech only: weight, water, elastic, the dam and launch combos, the procession, one boss, the village. The highest-risk systems used in chapters 2-4 are never built before production: layered holes (cellar/tunnel), wind cones pushing objects and the gliding player, moving platforms you can ride (puffed mushroom, floating on a wave, cloud island, sinking floor with a rider, the walking giant), 90° camera-zone rotation, tide moving the water range, light cones with mirror reflection, and dark spaces. The measured per-type costs won't predict those chapters. The perf check uses 'a dense greybox', which doesn't represent final procedural art with outlines, particles and NPCs. The old game has never been measured on a Deck (docs/STEAM_RELEASE.md still has the Deck check unticked).
issues.fix: Add a weeks 4-6 'tech spike' list, each item a no-art greybox room: ⑥ cellar via a portal, wind push + glide, a puff ride (moving platform), a camera-zone yaw change, a tide state change, a 2×3 procession with a straw flag. In week 1, run the existing packaged Linux build on a real Deck as a baseline, and confirm the owner has a Deck. At week 6, measure a synthetic worst-case scene on the Deck (about 150 Pluckables of 40 types with hulls, 12 bearers, 20 animals, particles, medium shadows) instead of a greybox.

issues.problem: '10 h/week of play and judging' is the only owner budget. Not budgeted: reviewing art for about 150 procedural object types plus about 24 neighbours plus 4 bosses, which HANDOFF §8 requires to not look AI-made; capsule A/B with 3 characters; 2 batches of 12 shorts; Wholesome Direct and streamer outreach; the 12-step trademark checks; a publisher/port deck; Discord and community; localisation QA for 4 languages; recruiting testers and watching 2 sessions per week. At 7 weeks per chapter, with 2 weeks of puzzle iteration, 10 h/week leaves only a few hours for level judgement after tester sessions.
issues.fix: State the owner's total weekly hours and split them (for example play/judge 10, art review 4-5, marketing/community 4-6, admin 2). Give art review a batch rhythm using the existing src/render/dev/model-gallery.ts (one gallery pass per week, accept/reject rows). Move marketing production into explicit calendar blocks in §20-7. Treat 'owner hours per accepted zone' as a measured vertical-slice metric next to the agent-time metrics.

issues.problem: Weeks 1-2 are overloaded, and week 3 mixes two questions. Week 1 builds the monorepo extraction in parallel with a feel build that depends on the extracted code. Week 2 swaps to the Ongi rig, runs the Deck face test, adds 8-12 objects, 2 tags, 2 rules, sparkle/grades/size records, the brand sound, telemetry, and starts a capsule A/B that needs 3 characters at capsule quality. Week 3 tests 'half raccoon first, half Ongi first' inside the feel gate. With n=5, character order adds noise to the two hard feel gates.
issues.fix: Build the feel test inside the new monorepo from day 1, pulling old files in on demand behind a small 'compat types' shim (that shim is the extraction). Run the week-3 feel gate with Ongi only. Compare raccoon vs Ongi through silhouette/clip/capsule tests in weeks 4-6, since the decision isn't needed until week 6. Move capsule art for the three characters to weeks 4-5.

issues.problem: The budget is right but the rules that make it achievable are missing. Every Pluckable gets a permanent ink outline, and the existing outline is an inverted-hull child mesh per source mesh (src/render/models/outline.ts), which doubles draws and needs an instanced hull material. Procedural models in the old kit use several materials and parts per model, so 'one InstancedMesh per type' becomes parts × materials × (main + hull + shadow) draws. three.js culls an InstancedMesh as a whole, not per instance. Terrain cell states (wet, frozen, ice, frost spreading, tide, sinking floor) change at runtime and would rebuild merged terrain. Idle animation on instanced objects (sway, flinch before resistance, wheels) needs per-instance attributes. §18-3/§20-4 offer WebGPURenderer as the fallback, but WebGPU in Electron on Linux/SteamOS is not a dependable fallback.
issues.fix: Add rules: one merged geometry + one toon material (vertex colour/atlas) per Pluckable type; instanced hull outline sharing the instance buffer; triangle caps per tier (S ≤ 600, M ≤ 2k, L ≤ 6k, XL ≤ 12k, characters ≤ 3k); shadow-map casters only L/XL/characters (S/M use blob shadows); instancing chunked per 8×8 cells for culling; terrain cell state read from a per-cell DataTexture so terrain merges once; per-instance 'anim phase/amplitude' attributes for idle motion. Replace the WebGPU fallback with render-scale (0.75), shadows off, and the 40 Hz mode.

issues.problem: There are many moving platforms you can stand on, which kinematic controllers handle worst. The puffed mushroom drifts in wind with Ongi riding it. A wave carries floating objects and Ongi. The cloud island is carried by the procession with sheep on it. The thin floor sinks over 6 s with a rider. The iron-stake giant walks the city and is climbed 'via launch, steam column and puff'. The walking 4×4 XL giant also breaks the camera-side 1.5 m rule (§16-3) and the procession/clearance graph. The doc has no rider rules.
issues.fix: Step every moving surface cell by cell on the grid with tweens, attach riders by cell (the rider inherits the platform's transform and jump is locked during a tween), and forbid free continuous platform motion. Redesign the giant fight so the giant walks along an authored rail between stations and kneels, stationary, during climb segments. Each kneel gives a static walkable deck, and the camera locks to a framed shot there.

issues.problem: Autosave fires on every place, pluck, zone move and every 60 s, but there is no rule for transient states: a plank mid-sink, an 8 s rainbow bridge, a 20 s fog clearing, a pending 15 s broom-dokkaebi revert, a tide mid-cycle, a boulder chase, a boulder mid-roll or mid-throw, NPCs mid-settle. Saves also store object state per zone, keyed to level JSON ids. When a content patch renames or removes an object or reshapes a zone, older saves can soft-lock, which breaks the 'never betray' promise.
issues.fix: Autosave only at quiescent ticks (no active tweens or timers). On load, resolve each timer to its authored rest state: a plank finishes sinking, a bridge collapses, fog returns, a broom revert is cancelled. Give every zone a content hash and keep object ids stable. If the hash changes, reset that zone's layout to the authored state and keep all progress (stage, dokkaebi, neighbours, codex, opened doors). Add a CI test that loads saves from the previous build into the current one.

issues.problem: At pitch 50°, 9-12 m distance and the old 38° FOV, the view covers about 10-13 × 8-11 cells. The sample zone is 16×12, the lighthouse cone is 8 cells, the windmill gust is 6 cells plus a rotating cone, and the boss arenas are larger, so puzzles often won't fit on screen. A 90° yaw change at a camera-zone boundary also remaps the stick in the middle of a step. The 1.5 m camera-side rule effectively forces every level to climb away from the camera.
issues.fix: Let each camera zone set its own distance and framing (puzzle rooms frame the whole puzzle). Keep the old input mapping until the stick returns to neutral after a yaw change. Use the right-stick look-ahead in puzzle rooms. Add a 'camera frames the puzzle' check to the preview (below).

issues.problem: The unit behind 'one greybox zone in 2 days' is unclear: a zone is a 10-15 minute 4-stage block, while the sample map is a 16×12 room. The preview extends tools/layout-svg.ts, a 2D SVG, so it won't show real camera occlusion or the camera-side rule. Ruling out any in-game editor also rules out a cheap dev-only nudge tool, and that tool is where most puzzle-tuning time goes.
issues.fix: Define the units: room = one stage beat, 2 days to a playable greybox; zone = 3-4 rooms, about 1 week. Render previews with the real three.js view from each camera zone, headless, through the existing playwright/view-harness. Allow a dev-build-only 'drag object on grid → write JSON' tool, and make clear that only the player-facing editor is permanently out. Hot-reload level files into the running build.

issues.problem: The extraction is real decoupling, not copying. uproot.ts imports LootState, Simulation, BANK_MODEL and SAFE_SPECS from ../sim plus BANK_POP and SAFE_POP. feel.ts imports SimEvent and Simulation. raccoon.ts imports CharacterLook, TeamId and TEAM_STYLES. input.ts imports Command and DT. save.ts (1390 lines) is mostly the old match schema, so only its migration pattern carries over. Reuse saves maybe 6-10 weeks of infrastructure and none of the bottleneck work (levels, tuning, playtests). The '40-50%' figure shouldn't be read as schedule savings.
issues.fix: On day 1, create a small 'compat' types package (Vec2, ids, quality preset) and port each module behind an adapter, starting with uproot driven by {progress, tension, popped} and feel driven by new events. Treat save as new code that keeps the old versioned-migration pattern. In §19-2, state reuse as infrastructure time saved, not a share of the remake's work.

issues.problem: '50 or more fresh testers' undercounts. Week 3 needs 2×5, then the grammar test 5 (+5 on a re-check), the vertical slice 5 (+5), each of 4 chapters 5 (+5), the demo 30+, plus silhouette (5), 10-second clip (10), screenshot and capsule tests, and from the vertical slice on, 2 sessions per week. That is roughly 90-120 fresh people plus returning testers for the 2-hour continuation gate.
issues.fix: Size the pipeline at about 100 fresh testers plus a returning pool of about 15. Use unmoderated recorded sessions plus telemetry for most rounds and live observation only for gate rounds, and track 'fresh testers left in the pool' as a schedule risk in §25.

issues.problem: 'A console port becomes a renderer rewrite, not a game rewrite' understates it. The DOM/HTML UI, the procedural WebAudio engine, the Gamepad API input, save/steam and the Electron shell all need rewriting too. Only the pure-TS puzzle sim carries over.
issues.fix: Reword to 'the sim and level data carry over; renderer, UI, audio and platform layers are rewritten'. Keep the porting-partner route.

issues.problem: Where telemetry goes is unspecified: the backend, consent UI, retention, a privacy note on the store page, and how Steam Playtest builds upload.
issues.fix: For playtest builds, write telemetry to local JSONL that is uploaded after explicit consent to one simple endpoint (or exported by the tester). Strip it from release builds, or make it opt-in with a privacy notice. Budget about 2-3 days.

eval:production.v1IssuesResolved: Production/tech issues from v1 (13 total). (1) CRITICAL full scope doesn't fit: PARTIAL. Chapters cut, schedule is itemised and moved to month 17-18, re-forecast after the vertical slice. But density per chapter rose about 2-3x and the 7-week basis wasn't re-priced; the buffer is about 8%. (2) CRITICAL no level-authoring pipeline: LARGELY RESOLVED (grid, text/JSON, preview, solver, the 2-day check). Still open: the heightfield can't express cellars, tunnels, ceilings, bridges or object tops; the solver isn't tractable as written and check 3 always passes; no dev nudge tool. (3) Engine/platform: RESOLVED by the owner's Steam-only decision (web stack kept, fallbacks named). (4) Save vs regrowth vs tags: RESOLVED at the rule level (§15-3/15-4/15-5). New open items: saving mid-timer states and keeping content ids stable across patches. (5) Uneven reaction/hole costs: RESOLVED structurally (A/B/C tiers, caps, 6 prefabs, cheap variants). Partial: several A rows hide secondary actors, and the actor layer (neighbours, animals, NPC rules) is unpriced. (6) Procession/dokkaebi/gravity one-liners: MOSTLY RESOLVED (authored graph, conditional edges, wait points, shared boss state machine, gravity at object level only). Open: straw flag to any cell vs an authored graph, footprint clearance, crossing zones, the walking climbable giant. (7) Rigid-body physics: RESOLVED (§16-4). Open: rules for moving platforms you can ride. (8) Gates stall the schedule: RESOLVED (2 hard gates per phase, counts, re-check, telemetry, tester pipeline). Partial: tester volume undercounted (about 100, not 50). (9) three.js performance with movable objects: PARTIAL. There is a budget, instancing and a harness. Missing: merged-geometry/material and hull-outline rules, a terrain cell-state approach, worst-case measurement on a real Deck. The WebGPU fallback isn't credible on SteamOS. (10) Camera with height: MOSTLY RESOLVED (fixed yaw, 90° zones, vertical lock during jumps, blob shadow, 1.5 m rule). Open: framing the whole puzzle at 9-12 m, stick remap on yaw change. (11) Determinism: RESOLVED (§19-5). (12) Wishes as text, 15 promised and only 5 defined: RESOLVED (10 pictogram wishes, 1-week system). (13) Repo strategy: RESOLVED (new monorepo, path-level reuse table, leave-behind list). Partial: the coupling to the old sim is deeper than 'copy' suggests, and week-1 extraction runs alongside the feel build that depends on it.
topRecommendations: Re-price chapters for v2's density before committing to dates. Plan 9-10 weeks per chapter until the vertical slice measures otherwise, add a content-days line per chapter, raise the buffer to 15-20%, and count the 2027 holidays. Either accept a release build around April-May 2028 or decide the trims now: garnish 66→40, variants 23→12, named neighbours about 24→16 on 2-3 shared body templates, scene cards about 40→25.

Fix the world model before the format freezes. Areas become several heightfield 'decks' linked by portals, hole prefabs ⑤/⑥ open authored sub-room decks, and objects that have height declare walkable tops. Prototype a cellar, a tunnel pair, a ceiling cell and a bridge as greybox in weeks 4-6.

Add a weeks 4-6 tech-spike list so the vertical slice's measured costs predict chapters 2-4: wind push + glide, a puffed-mushroom ride (moving platform with grid-stepped rider rules), a 90° camera-zone change with stick remap held until neutral, a tide state change, a 2×3 procession to a straw flag on an auto-generated clearance graph. Run the existing packaged build on a real Deck in week 1, and measure a synthetic worst-case final-art scene on the Deck at week 6.

Make the solver bot tractable and useful. Search only puzzle-relevant objects, resolve NPC rules through a deterministic settle function, model timers as open/closed windows, change check 3 to 'goal reachable without the stump', report near-dead-end states, and set CI time budgets per area. Generate procession graphs from the grid and keep only wait points hand-authored.

Budget all of the owner's time, not just play. Give explicit weekly hours for art review (model-gallery batches), marketing (capsules, 2×12 shorts, showcases, trademark), testers and admin. Size the tester pipeline at about 100 fresh testers. Keep the week-3 feel gate to Ongi only, and move the raccoon/badger comparison and capsule A/B to weeks 4-6.

Write the perf rules into §18-3: one merged geometry and one toon material per type, an instanced hull outline, triangle caps per tier, shadow-map casters only L/XL/characters, chunked instancing, a per-cell DataTexture for terrain state, per-instance idle-animation attributes. Replace the WebGPU fallback with render-scale and the 40 Hz mode. In §15-3, add quiescent-only autosave, timers that resolve on load, and per-zone content hashes with a layout-reset fallback.

eval:consistency.verdict: This lens is internal consistency and a rule audit. v2 is a big step up from v1. Almost every structural contradiction the v1 audit raised is fixed, and fixed with concrete numbers rather than new words. That covers the paw/chapter mismatch, the chapter-0 tutorial that taught the wrong colour rule, the 4-3 'every visible root is pluckable' rule, the procession teleport, save vs regrowth, randomness and the S-tier split. The 손힘 checklist (6-2), the 6x6 matrix (8-2), the formula table (5-3) and the save table (15-3) are the kind of thing a solver bot can actually check. I re-ran the 5-3 tug formulas and they broadly reproduce the published timings and hold/slip outcomes. Several of my skilled or normal times came out longer, though (메기 XL 보통 7.2s vs 6.0s), so the table is close but not exact. v2 also adds a lot of new systems, and most of what is left sits where those systems meet: entourage vs rules 3/5/8, procession vs chapter routing, stump/cart/regrow vs no-duplication, held tags vs combos, and placement rules vs 발사. One contradiction blocks the critical path as written. The 우산버섯 is an M object, and M cannot be carried in a jump before stage 3, yet chapter 2 (stage 2) and the windmill's third eye both need you to glide with it. A dozen rules also need one more sentence each before the 6-week grammar gate, or they will show up as "왜 이건 안 돼?" in playtests. None of this needs a redesign. It needs a v2.1 errata pass.
strengths: Paw gating fixed properly: one unit (손힘 단계 0~5), one number per tier (S=0, M=1, L=2, XL=4), stage 1 from the pear tree, release pulls exempt from the paw check, and a 데려올 것 점검표 that checks every item against the stage at that moment (6-2). I re-walked it and found no tier violations except the glide/toss issues below.

The chapter 0 refusals now teach correct and separate lessons: the brown 우체통 is paid off 7 minutes later, the silver 곳간 on a revisit, and the rainbow pear tree with ●●○ silhouettes (12-3, 6-3). That removes v1's worst tutorial contradiction.

4-3 is rewritten honestly: 'no permanent refusals' plus exactly four readable locks, a 붙박이 장식 class with concrete visual rules (no outline, plinth, no shared meshes), and an audit that requires every object to reach an unlock state (6-3, 6-4, 6-6).

The tag system is now auditable: a full 6x6 matrix with 7 explicit no-ops, same-tag rules on the diagonal, ranges in cells measured from the footprint edge, held-tag ranges, no tag strengths, and 'combo outputs are not tags' (8-1, 8-2). The 20-1 count (8 + 7 + 6) checks out.

Randomness is scoped correctly: inputs and resistance are deterministic, rewards are authored, the 툭 delays are fixed per type, the pity timer is gone, the big turnip is tied to water range, and size is a function of score (5-1, 5-4, 9-2 rule 6).

Pulling is fully specified: the hook outcome, the progress/tension formula, slip at 0.3 s over the limit, '손이 익었다' with numbers, line-up as an ordinary pull with a 1.3 limit and no beat judgement, and finale difficulty fixed (5-2~5-6). I re-ran the formula myself and got the same success/slip pattern for '계속 꾹'.

The procession now separates geometry blocks (wait point, residents point, condition edges judged by property) from AI faults (teleport only along open edges), with 1 active procession and a quit rule (7-4).
Save, regrowth and stump are separated: per-zone object state, opened paths never close, original objects never regrow, and the stump resets placement only, never progression (15-3~15-5).

The input contract covers most v1 holes: latched carry, hold-and-release throw, facing = placement direction, branch on grade rather than press length, jump = no-penalty cancel during a pull, and an analog trigger as pull depth (4-2).
Wishes are latched, written as terrain-independent relations, every village site gets a pond, hill, plaza and road, and there is a pre-finale village step for 단단 (13-1, 13-3, 12-7).
The capsule is now true under the rules thanks to the 1-second hoist (7-4, 21-3). The chapter 4 'houses tilt, never collapse' rule finally makes the constitution and the story agree (12-7).

The internal numbers mostly reconcile: archetype cost tally 16/7/6/2, 곁들이 10+14+14+16+12=66, variants 23, chapter minutes 237 + village 22 + festival 5 = 264, and the per-chapter counts of new rules and combos in 10-4 match 8-4 and 9-2.
Section 24 keeps the six videos explicitly pending rather than inventing their content, as the brief required.

issues.problem: Gliding is impossible when the game requires it. 우산버섯 is M (10-1 #16). 16-2 says '활공 | 우산버섯을 들고 점프', but the same table and 4-2 say 'M 들고 불가 (손힘 3단계부터 0.6m)'. Stage 3 is granted only by freeing the chapter 2 windmill (6-2). Yet 2-2's 응용 is '우산버섯 활공으로 틈 건너기', and the windmill's third eye is '우산버섯으로 활공해 지붕 축에 내려앉아', both at stage 2. As written, chapter 2 cannot be finished. The paw checklist missed it because it only checks plucks, not carry verbs.
issues.fix: Pick one and write it into 4-2 and 16-2. (a) Make 우산버섯 S, which is also more readable: a mushroom you lift overhead. (b) Add a carve-out: 'objects with the 활공 property can be carried into a jump at any stage (0.6m)'. Then extend the 6-2 checklist into a verb checklist (pluck / carry-jump / throw / glide / swim-with) per chapter, so the solver bot catches this class of bug.

issues.section: 2 (동행) vs 9-2 rules 3, 5, 8 vs 12-4 (1-1 졸업, 1-2 장난 구역) vs 9-3
issues.problem: The entourage collides with three system rules, and no input exists to resolve it. 동행 follow 옹이 everywhere (2: up to 6 on screen). Rule 8 ('그 물체 2칸 안에 이웃이 있으면 못 건드림') is then satisfied automatically whenever 옹이 is near, so the broom zone is trivial. Yet 1-2's intended answer is '밤톨을 옆에 세우거나', and there is no command for making a neighbour stand somewhere. Rule 5 ('2명 이상 같은 칸이나 같은 발판') means a trailing entourage can press plates by accident, or a single-file line never does; the formation is undefined. Rule 3 applies to '할 일 없는 이웃', but it is not said whether following counts as idle. 1-1 졸업 relies on '이웃들이 사과나무 그늘에 모여 쉬고 있음' while the chapter starts with 4 entourage members. Rule 4 has the same parking problem: freed chickens follow 옹이 off the plate.
issues.fix: Define it in one paragraph. While following, entourage and rule-4 followers are 'busy': they count for neither rule 5 nor rule 8. Add a parking verb that reuses an existing input. With no procession active, grab on empty ground plants a 짚 깃발, and followers gather and rest there; a flag on a plate presses it under rule 5, and a flag beside an object guards it under rule 8. Re-press to recall. Update 4-2, 7-4, 9-2 and the 1-2 beat to use it. Specify follower formation as 'cluster within 1 cell of the leader's last stop', not single file.

issues.section: 7-4 (1 active procession, 30~90 s segments, max 2 wait points) vs 12-5 2-2 졸업 / 2-4 / 6-5
issues.problem: Procession routing doesn't fit the chapter flow. The inn procession is 2-2's 졸업 at minute ~25. Its default destination is the 이사 문, which lies past 2-3 (fog) and 2-4 (windmill gusts, unsolved). It would sit at a wait point for about 25 minutes, breaking '행렬 구간은 한 번에 30~90초' and '대기 지점은 최대 2개'. Then at 2-4, '종각(L)을 뽑으면 … 이웃이 모두 달려와 행렬' starts a second procession while the inn's is still active, against '동시에 움직이는 행렬은 1개'. Nothing says what a parked procession is, whether its carriers are still busy, or what happens when you pluck another L while one is in progress. The same applies to 큰 거울 (L) in chapter 3, which must be both brought home and used for the lighthouse.
issues.fix: Add three rules. (1) A procession that reaches a wait point it cannot pass within the current zone auto-parks: it re-plants as a shallow-rooted L at that node, carriers disperse, and it no longer counts as active. Re-grabbing it resumes a short procession. (2) Plucking a new L/XL while one is moving makes the moving one auto-park first. (3) Authoring rule: every procession's route to its destination must be fully openable inside the current and already-cleared zones. Otherwise its default destination is the zone's flag spot, not the 이사 문. Move the inn's 이사 문 trip to after the windmill, as the v1 review suggested.

issues.section: 15-5 (stump) / 6-5 / 13-4 (cart) / 12-9 (tide) / 9-2 rule 8 / 15-4 vs 15-4 '복제·반복 수확 불가' and second law
issues.problem: The no-duplication and no-farming promises leak through return-to-origin paths. (a) The stump resets 'that zone's object placement' to the start, so a well or hot stone already sent home via the cart (6-5, 13-4), or an L already processioned out, would respawn: a duplicate. (b) The broom ('원래 자리로 쓸어다 다시 심음'), the tide ('아니면 원래 자리에 다시 돋음'), out-of-bounds regrowth and the stump all return objects to their origin, but nothing says whether they come back natively rooted (full pull, so size and shiny can be re-rolled, contradicting '기록을 반복 수확할 수 없다') or shallow-rooted. (c) An origin that is now an open passage hole ('열린 길은 닫히지 않는다') would get an object replanted on top of it.
issues.fix: Write one 'return' rule used by all four paths. A returned object always comes back shallow-rooted: instant re-pluck, no score, no sparkle, no shiny roll. If its origin cell is an open hole, it re-sprouts on the nearest valid cell beside the hole. Objects that left the zone (cart, procession, finished landmark) are flagged 'departed' in the zone save, and the stump never restores them.

issues.problem: Held tags have ranges (heat 1 cell, water 1 cell, wind 'as is, like a blower', light 'as is'), but nothing says whether held tags trigger combos. Undefined cases: holding a wind tree while floating means 물결 carries 옹이 herself, which is self-propulsion. Holding a hot stone (M) near water creates a steam column under 옹이; does she rise while holding an M? A carried lantern in a wind cone creates 회전 빛 in her hands. 'No chains' is defined at tag level only, not at object level. Can a rotating light's sweep across water make 무지개 다리? Does a 발사-launched weight that lands on a second mushroom launch again? Steam lifts 'S급'; where do they stop, and does a lifted S heat source over water spawn another column?
issues.fix: Add a held-tag row to the matrix. Proposed: held objects emit their range but never form combos (combos need both sources planted), except wind on 'floating' things, which never moves the carrier. Object-level chains: a launched object that lands on an elastic tile lands normally (no re-launch); a rotating light still counts as a light cone; steam lifts S to the column top and sets them on the nearest ledge cell at that height. Have the solver bot enumerate every combo × held/planted state.

issues.section: 7-2 (occupied cells unplaceable) / 7-3 (landing always on a valid cell, ±1 magnet) vs 8-2 발사 / 12-4 1-3 / 11-2 장승 ② / 12-7 4-2
issues.problem: 발사 is triggered when a weight object 'is placed on or dropped onto the elastic top'. But 7-2 lists '다른 물체' as an unplaceable cell, and only '평평' objects can be stacked on. 7-3 says landings snap to a valid empty cell within ±1. So a stone can neither be placed on nor thrown onto a mushroom; the magnet pushes it off. Chapter 1's third sub-gimmick (1-3), 장승 eye ② ('머리 위에 떨어뜨림' lands on an occupied dokkaebi) and 4-2 ('말뚝을 통통버섯에 떨어뜨려') all depend on this. Separately, nothing says whether 옹이 can stand on objects, which 'step on the mushroom' (0장 2:30) requires.
issues.fix: Add an object 'top surface' class: 탄성 and 평평 objects accept placement and throw landings on top, and the throw magnet prefers these tops within ±1. A dokkaebi's head counts as a landing target for its eye conditions. Add one row to 16-2: 옹이 can stand on S/M objects whose height is ≤0.5m; others block.

issues.problem: The shiny variant set cannot be completed, and parts of it can be missed permanently. 6 archetypes are S and have no pull, so they can never score 딱!. Line-up has no 툭 ('없음 (바로 시작)'), so the 40-point hook is impossible, max score is 60, and the pear tree and 대말뚝 can never be 딱!. That is 8 of 31 unreachable. Single-instance objects (곳간, 물레방아, 여관, 종각, 상점, 고목, 구름섬, 시계탑, 수레) are pulled exactly once, and player-placed objects re-pluck instantly (7-2), so missing 딱! once is permanent. After stage 5, all M/L become '쏙' with the result fixed at 좋음, which kills the remaining shinies post-game. Also, 5-3 lists a 숙련 time for 줄 서기 that assumes a hook line-up can't have. And 17-3's 도우미 says '기록은 그대로 남는다' without saying whether assisted pulls can reach 딱!.
issues.fix: Count shinies over 'kinds that use a pull' only (23), or give S kinds a shiny through a different authored route. Let '쏙' and stage 5 skip the pull only when the shiny is already owned, or allow an opt-in full pull by holding the grab. For one-off landmarks, either count shiny as 좋음+ or let the stump of that zone offer one re-pull. Fix the 5-3 line-up row to 'no hook' timings. State that assisted pulls cap at 좋음, so records stay skill-based.

issues.problem: The store's core promise ('with the family still inside') conflicts with the general rules. 7-3: '이웃이 타고 있는 물체(벤치와 할아버지)는 잡는 순간 이웃이 먼저 폴짝 내린다', repeated in 1-1 ('벤치를 잡으면 할아버지가 폴짝 내림'). But 10-1 #11's gag is '앉아 있던 할아버지가 딸려 올라옴', and the trailer shows '할아버지 탄 벤치'. Rule 1 says owners follow their plucked house on foot. So 'family inside' happens only in the one scripted 4-3 beat and in #19's first-time gag. The capsule and GIF ① sell something the rules forbid in general.
issues.fix: Write a riding rule. Neighbours stay aboard anything that goes into a procession or a 1-second hoist (houses, benches lifted by pluck), and hop off only when a throw is aimed or the object is placed. Rule 1 then becomes 'the owner rides inside or walks beside it' (data flag per house). Align 7-3, the 1-1 beat and #11 to that rule.

issues.section: 9-2 rule 4 / 11-1 '동행에 합류' vs 13-4 'L·XL은 행렬로만 온다' / 2 이웃 정의 / 13-2
issues.problem: Freed dokkaebi are 'returned to their original object, becoming neighbours who join the entourage' and 'follow 옹이 in a line' under rule 4. But the windmill and lighthouse are XL 3x3, the giant is XL 4x4 and the 장승 is L. An XL entourage on a 1m grid with 1m steps and narrow paths contradicts 'L·XL come only by procession' and the procession graph. Section 2 defines 이웃 as 'NPC with a name and a wish', but 13-2 lists five main-path neighbours without wishes (두루, 밤톨, 등대, 시계탑지기, 거인), and optional neighbours have '소원은 없고'. 11-1 says every freed dokkaebi gains a wish, but 등대 and 거인 have '—'. The bench 할아버지 and the 연맹 residents who line up in the finale are not in 13-2, so whether they count toward N is unclear.
issues.fix: Redefine 이웃 = named NPC who counts toward population, with the wish optional. Freed L/XL dokkaebi become a procession object (their body) plus a small spirit actor that joins the entourage, or they go straight to the village via the 이사 문 procession. List every population-counting NPC in 13-2 (including the bench grandfather and 연맹 households) and state which count toward N=14.

issues.problem: M can be thrown farther, earlier, through the back door. The 쑥! over-the-shoulder toss sends an M 2/3/4 cells by grade from stage 1. M throwing is locked until stage 3, and then only 3 cells. So a 딱! pull gives a 4-cell M throw at stage 1. Nothing says whether toss landings may change height level (onto a ledge or across a gap), so this can bypass puzzles built around 'M can't be thrown or jumped yet' (all of chapters 1-2). 5-4's 'puzzles are always solvable without tossing' guards solvability, not sequence breaks.
issues.fix: Cap the toss at 2 cells, same height level or lower, until stage 3, then use the grade distances. Or keep the distances but forbid toss landings on a higher level or across non-walkable cells. Add the toss to the solver bot's macro actions.

issues.problem: Wind pushes 옹이 by one rule and not by another. 8-1 and rule 7: wind pushes 'weightless S on the ground and 옹이 while gliding'. But 2-2's 소개 is '강풍 절벽길에서 밀려남' and the windmill's gust 'pushes 옹이 and S'. Both push a walking 옹이. It is also unstated whether the windmill gust is a wind tag (needed for '마주 보는 바람나무로 상쇄' and 바람막이 to work) with a non-standard range (6-cell rotating cone).
issues.fix: Either add 'walking 옹이 in a wind cone is pushed 1 cell/s' to 8-1 (and check the 2-1 blower verb against it), or make 강풍/돌풍 a separate hazard. Then say explicitly that the windmill gust is a wind tag with a dokkaebi-only range and rotation, so cancellation and 바람막이 apply by the matrix.

issues.problem: Tag occlusion and height are undefined in a diorama with 0.5m levels. Only weight objects block wind ('무게 물체 뒤 3칸은 바람이 없음'), so a big untagged house gives no shelter: a textbook 'why doesn't this work?'. It is not said whether wind and light cones pass over or under level changes, through objects, or into the upper cells of steam columns; whether a light cone hitting a house stops; or which cell an L/XL cone originates from (mirror L 2x2, lighthouse XL 8 cells).
issues.fix: Add a 'blocks cones' column to the archetype sheet (default: any L/XL and any weight object block wind; any opaque object blocks light; S never blocks). Cones are 2D on the grid, travel across height differences ≤0.5m and stop at higher walls. The origin is the front-centre footprint cell. Add the rule to the audit.

issues.section: 16-1 '칸 하나는 높이 하나' vs 10-3 ⑤ 굴, ⑥ 지하실 / 10-1 #21 나무 다리 / 3-3 천장 칸 / 증기·부풂
issues.problem: The single-height-per-cell world model can't represent content the doc relies on. Tunnels ('두 구멍을 잇는 짧은 굴') run under other cells. Bridges (나무 다리, condition edges over water) need walkable cells above water cells. Cellars sit under ground cells. The ceiling layer is patched in as an exception ('천장 칸 층'). Steam tops (3m), 부풂 platforms (1m up) and hanging objects add more vertical stacking. The level text format in 19-3 has only one height grid.
issues.fix: Make the model explicit: a base height grid plus a small set of layers (underground spaces as separate sub-zones entered through holes, overhead decks for bridges, the ceiling layer). Or reduce tunnels and cellars to 'hole leads to a separate mini-zone'. Update the 19-3 format and the solver bot's state accordingly.

issues.problem: Rule 3 only knows two cases: '한낮 → 그늘, 아침·노을 → 빛 범위'. But chapter 2 is 늦은 오후, chapter 4 is 흐린 한낮 → 맑음, and the finale is 해 질 녘, so rule 3 is undefined for two main chapters and the finale. The lighthouse eye ③ is '큰 거울로 노을빛을 꺾어', but sunlight is not a light-tag source anywhere in 8-1. Meanwhile the mirror carries its own 빛 tag plus a 반사 property, so it is unclear whether it emits a cone by itself (which would make reflection pointless) or only bends incoming light. 8-3's 'light works in dark spaces' also contradicts rule 3 and the open-air rainbow bridge.
issues.fix: Give each chapter a rule-3 mode in 12-1 (shade / light). Remove the 빛 tag from the mirror and keep only 반사, and add one authored 'sunbeam' light source per chapter 3 zone (a shaft from the sunset with a fixed cone) if eye ③ should stay. Reword 8-3 to say 'revealing hidden roots requires light'; the light tag itself works everywhere.

issues.problem: Several mechanics have no input. Rule 9 triggers on '뽑거나 놓거나 치면', but there is no strike or ring action. 쌍가락 매듭 holds two S in two hands with 'two throws in a row', but which one places first and how the preview shows two items is undefined. Village layout (13-1) moves L/XL and sets facing (wishes #2 and #6 depend on facing) with no stated input. Hanging objects under the cloud overhang (3-3) are plucked from below with no reach rule. Before stage 3, a long press while holding an M (throw locked) is undefined.
issues.fix: Drop '치면' from rule 9 or define it as 'grab on a 부름 object you already placed = ring'. 쌍가락: the first press places or throws the left-hand item, and the preview shows the next item. The village uses the same carry/place verbs, with L/XL moved by a mini-procession to a flag, or a menu cursor with rotate on the bumpers; write which. Hanging objects can be grabbed from the cell directly below when their base is ≤1.5m above 옹이. Long press with an un-throwable M simply places it.

issues.problem: Targeting and keyboard parity gaps. 'Rotate in place' requires 'stick below 35%', which WASD cannot produce, so keyboard players can't choose a placement facing without stepping. Grab target selection is never defined (front cell? nearest? priority among S 곁들이, a lock, empty ground?). That matters because 'grab on empty ground while a procession moves = plant the 짚 깃발', so a slightly off grab near 곁들이 either plucks or re-routes the procession. 6-5 says L/XL go to '짚 깃발 자리', which reads as authored spots, while 7-4 allows any empty ground. Re-flagging while the procession waits is not covered either, because the input row says '움직이는 중' only.
issues.fix: Keyboard: hold a modifier (or tap a direction while holding 잡기 still) to turn without moving. Define grab targeting: the front cell first, then front-diagonals, with objects winning over empty ground, and the flag only when the front cell is empty and walkable. Choose one flag rule (any empty walkable cell in the zone), and allow flagging while the procession is moving or waiting.

issues.problem: Neighbour wandering is undefined and may be random. Wandering neighbours affect rule 5 (weight), rule 8 (guard within 2 cells) and procession blocking (9-3's bridge example). If wander paths are random, puzzle outcomes vary, which breaks '같은 입력이면 언제나 같은 결과'. The solver bot's macro actions (뽑기, 놓기+방향, 던지기, 짚 깃발) also leave out jump, glide, swim, steam rides, the 쑥! toss and every timed actor (broom 15 s, tide 90 s, fog 20 s, 8 s bridge, the walking giant), so check 3 ('막힘이 없는가') cannot be trusted for the zones that use them.
issues.fix: Make wandering deterministic (authored loops per zone), and say wanderers never count for rules 5 and 8. Only resting actors (rules 2 and 3) or parked followers count. Extend the bot with traversal macros and a discrete-time model for timed actors (or mark those zones 'manual verification required' in CI).

issues.problem: 9-3's example 'clearing the apple tree at the bridge moves the neighbours resting in its shade, so the procession can cross' implies idle neighbours block procession edges. But 7-4 recruits every neighbour into the procession ('동행 이웃과 마을 이웃이 달려와 대상 밑으로'), and 놀람(행렬) has top priority. So resting neighbours would join the procession instead of blocking it.
issues.fix: Either drop the example, or say only non-population actors (animals, 연맹 workers) block edges, and that procession recruitment pulls neighbours from rest. Add the case to the 7-4 condition-edge rules: 'actors standing on an edge cell step aside unless sleeping animals'.

issues.problem: Weight quantity is undefined although plates use counts. 1-1 has a '추 둘 그림이 있는 큰 발판' solved by an M bench, and the level JSON has 'weight': 1, so S and M must have different weight values. Rule 5 says crowds '무게 판정' without saying how many units. 8-2's diagonal '무게+무게 = 합집합' implies union, not sum. Whether 옹이 herself weighs anything is not said. Players will stand on every plate in the first minute, so that one rule decides whether it reads as 'why doesn't this work?' or a broken puzzle.
issues.fix: Add a weight table: S weight-tag = 1, M weight-tag = 2, L/XL weight-tag = 3, a crowd of 2+ = 1, 옹이 = 0 (with a visible 'too light' wobble of the plate when she steps on it). Plates show their requirement as 추 icons. Change the 무게+무게 cell to 'sum on plates'.

issues.problem: The wrist thread carries five conflicting meanings: stage colour, always on (3-2, 6-2); grade colour only while pulling (3-2 '등급 색은 당길 때 손목 실에서만'); tension 'cream to red' (5-3, 3-7), which can't start from cream if the stage colour is the base; 손이 익었다 thickness (5-5); and knot shape (14-2). It is also gold or red at stage 4 and at the tension limit, which collides with 'gold + red is 옹이-only'.
issues.fix: Split the channels: the thread colour shows the stage, the glow intensity or straw bristles show tension, the number of wraps shows 손이 익었다, and the knot is a separate bead. Remove the 'grade colour on the wrist' line, since grade is already read from the root.

issues.problem: Actor and transient state isn't saved, although actors are puzzle pieces: rule-4 followers, sleeping animals holding a plate, parked entourage, tilted houses in chapter 4 (the state list is 'rooted, held, placed, sunk', no 'tilted'), the giant's position, and the tide phase. 'Held' is saved, but where 옹이 resumes, and therefore where a held item ends up after loading at a shelter, is not.
issues.fix: Add an actor list per zone (position, rule state, follow target), a 'tilted' object state and timed-cycle phases to 15-3. On load at a shelter, a held object re-plants shallow at 옹이's last valid placement cell.

issues.section: 6-3 / 6-6 audit vs 10-1 #21 / 8-1 & 16-4 thin floor / 15-5 stump / 12-4 1-1 gate
issues.problem: Several pluckables sit outside the grammar and the data sheet. The two-root bridge ('양쪽 끝 뿌리를 차례로 풀어야 뽑힘') adds a partial-refusal state that is not one of the four locks. Make the bridge's ends two separate S/M roots that must be plucked first (a stake-like sub-lock with its own visual) or drop the mechanic. issues.problem: Revisit processions have no destination. The 옛 곳간 (chapter 0, after 1) and 고목 (chapter 2, after 3) go by procession to 'that chapter's 이사 문', but the village has already moved on. As written, every drop down a ledge with an S in hand teleports and strips the item.

issues.problem: 11-2 says the residents 'must' be made safe before each giant stake is pulled, but 12-7's only consequence is that they tilt and sulk and refuse line-up. issues.fix: Define 'tallest' as absolute top height including terrain (the hill always allows it), or as 'tallest within 3 cells of the plaza'. Remove the 3-4 mention. Define 물 칸 = water terrain cell or any water-tag-covered cell, and use it everywhere.
